question.question: Can a leader demoted to learner with StepDownOnRemoval=false incorrectly use the singleton ReadIndex shortcut and authorize a stale local read after the remaining voter completes a later write, even if the caller advances strictly beyond the returned read index?
question.importance: Potential violation of the documented ReadOnlySafe linearizable-read responsibility when voter eligibility and retained leader role disagree; no completed stale-read witness exists yet.
participants: Read caller and replicated state-machine consumer
contexts: Joint configuration safely demotes old leader to learner
Network delays keep old leader unaware of new authority when read is admitted
event_paths: Commit and apply demotion -> finalize joint change -> isolate demoted leader -> remaining voter elects and commits write -> old leader ReadIndex -> limited later replication advances application past returned index but possibly before write

counterevidence: StepDownOnRemoval=true steps the demoted leader down and may prevent shortcut access.
A response index below a completed write is not itself a stale completed read: the explicit application boundary must be attained.

Receiving higher-term replication changes the old leader role and drops old-term network responses; the proposed discriminator uses a previously returned local ReadState whose caller has not yet consumed it.
Removed nodes are not automatically assumed to remain valid clients; using a demoted learner retains a documented replication role.
